variants.title: Advancing
variants.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: an individual alternative POSE of the approved classical cathedral stone statue, for later CL3D reconstruction.
Input image: design and identity reference. Preserve this SAME clearly adult woman, mature facial features, wavy pinned-back hair, graceful classical anatomy, bare shoulder, elegant plain drapery, small plain oval hand mirror, loose serpent and broken theatrical mask at the integral base. Preserve the aged pale warm-grey marble, fine Renaissance sculptural quality and understated symbolism.
Primary edit: substantially change the full-body pose as described below. This is a different sculpted position of the same character, not a camera-angle variation. Rearrange drapery naturally for the new pose. Keep the face recognizable and the body proportions consistent. Her expression is thoughtful and introspective. The mirror is plain carved stone. The serpent stays loosely coiled entirely on the base, separate from her body. The mask rests on the same base.
Composition: ONE complete sculpture on its small integral plain base, one view only, gentle near-frontal three-quarter camera. All limbs and complete base visible, generous margin; choose a framing that suits the new silhouette. Neutral diffuse studio lighting with gentle raking light, clear middle tones.
Construction: balanced plausible weight and supportive carved masses; solid drapery can connect to the base, robust fingers, no floating props. The design is wholly inanimate marble, all clothing and skin-looking areas sculpted from the same stone. The drapery fully covers breasts and pelvis. Figurative museum art.
Background: preserve genuine transparent alpha around the silhouette and through gaps. Clean stone-colored edges, no colored outlines or floor plane.
Avoid: changing her identity or hairstyle, extra people, a cathedral backdrop, ornate costume, Gothic tracery, patterned garment borders, jewelry, lettering, watermarks, multiple views, detached limbs, extra arms or fingers, theatrical effects or colored lighting.
New pose: She takes one measured forward step with her left foot placed clearly ahead and her right heel slightly raised. Her hips and shoulders counter-rotate gracefully; the mirror is held low against her left ribs and her right hand gathers a flowing fold at the opposite hip. Upright walking silhouette, head turned gently toward the forward shoulder, no standing-static contrapposto. The trailing mantle joins the back of the base for support.
